transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-05 11:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales, Priya Nair (Redwood); Liam Chen, Sofia Ruiz, Daniel Park (Arborient)

Auto Summary: quick head-to-head vs incumbent, p50 looks good, tail still needs work, try KV prefix warming and targeted quantization config; send security docs and pricing delta.

Topics: p50/p95 numbers, RPS/throughput, quantization tradeoffs, caching, routing fallback, next steps

00:00 - Ethan: alright hey everyone thanks for joining today, quick check, is this still 11 for you all?
00:07 - Liam: yep we're good, thanks Ethan
00:10 - Ethan: cool, agenda's short — go through last week's bench, surface the delta vs the incumbent provider you ran, and agree next bench to isolate the p95 cold start. Priya will jump into the numbers.
00:23 - Priya: hey all, so we ran the suite you dropped, 10 prompt templates, mix of short and long; key numbers — Redwood baseline config (4-bit QC, prefix cache on) p50 62ms, p95 310ms. Incumbent p50 88ms, p95 290ms on their reported logs. so median is better for us, tail is close, that's from roughly 2k samples across sessions.
00:49 - Sofia: wait you said p95 for you is slightly higher than incumbent? ours shows incumbent p95 270, you have 310 — that's a problem for bursty workloads.
00:58 - Priya: yeah so let me clarify, the incumbent numbers were mostly warm sessions; our run included a mix of cold starts to reflect real traffic, that pushes our p95 up. If we look warm-only p95, we drop to ~260ms. So cold-start is the delta.
01:17 - Daniel: can you define cold start here? like container spin up or KV miss?
01:22 - Priya: good q — our cold-start mix included empty KV-cache and first-token kernel init on GPU for the model variant. there is some overhead in kernel selection and quant table dispatch on the first few tokens.
01:34 - Ethan: to be explicit the model we used for these bench runs is the 7B quantized variant you green-lit, with continuous batching turned on at 10ms threshold, and prefix caching enabled when we detected repeated prefixes.
01:46 - Liam: why is continuous batching at 10ms? would increasing it reduce tail?
01:50 - Priya: yes increasing batch window raises throughput and can amortize the kernel init costs, but it also raises median latency for single requests. there's a tradeoff. For your SLOs you indicated 150ms median target during interactive flows, 500ms tail — are those still accurate?
02:05 - Liam: yes roughly, interactive agents need sub-150ms med ideally.
02:08 - Priya: ok then we should keep aggressive batching but focus on reducing cold-start p95 via two levers: KV prefix warming and dedicated slot for pods so warm state persists longer.
02:19 - Sofia: are we talking dedicated capacity — that's a cost increase. what's the delta vs incumbent?
02:24 - Ethan: that's fair — I'll put together a pricing delta. rough quick math: dedicated slot to keep a 7B quantized model warm is about 0.45x the incumbent per-hour for peak, because we leverage more aggressive quant and batching. but we'll send line-item details.
02:40 - Daniel: can you walk throughput numbers? our main concern is concurrent inference at peak; we saw 120 RPS from incumbent with 95th percentile latency at ~400ms.
02:49 - Priya: in our steady-state test, Redwood achieved ~190 RPS with the same CPU/GPU ratio when using dynamic batching and prefix reuse, with p95 around 320ms warm. the 190 number is with batching window at 10ms and batch size up to 32, and 4-bit quant. Without quant it's closer to 110 RPS.
03:14 - Sofia: so quantization alone doubled throughput? that seems high. can you explain the model quality tradeoffs?
03:19 - Priya: right, 4-bit quant reduces throughput and memory footprint — sorry, increases throughput and reduces memory, so yeah it was approx 1.6-1.8x in our runs. quality-wise we ran your eval set of 300 prompts; ROUGE/accuracy delta was within 1-2% on the tasks you shared. there are edge cases where hallucinations tick up slightly but nothing major in the set you gave.
03:42 - Liam: what's the failover story? if the dedicated slot isn't available we fall back to hosted. does that change latency dramatically?
03:48 - Ethan: our routing supports fallback to a compatible model variant in another region or to a slightly lower-precision quant variant. failover adds about 30-50ms network plus cold-start overhead if the destination is cold. we'll propose a canary/fallback policy that prefers region-local warm pools.
04:05 - Daniel: curious about KV cache — in our logs we saw 'KV cash' misses — are caches persistent between requests?
04:12 - Priya: yes KV cache is per-pod and persists as long as the slot remains warm; cold starts clear it. also our cache has an LRU eviction, so very long tails can evict some prefixes. We can offer targeted prefix warming for the top n templates you provide.
04:28 - Sofia: okay that sounds promising. what's required for prefix warming?
04:31 - Priya: you push the canonical prompts via a simple API or a one-off load job; we pre-populate KV for those templates and keep the pod warm for the maintenance window. that reduces first-token p95 by ~120ms in our tests.
04:45 - Liam: what about telemetry — we need token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns. do you expose that in the console?
04:51 - Ethan: yes Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route p50/p95, and tracing hooks you can attach; we'll add those dashboards to your trial account.
04:59 - Daniel: any security concerns with prefix data? some prompts include PHI.
05:04 - Priya: we support VPC peering and Private deployment; we also have KMS integration for key management. for the POC we'll redact sensitive tokens at ingestion and recommend using encrypted fields. We'll push SOC2 docs.
05:18 - Sofia: good. Can you also compare unit cost per response vs incumbent under similar batching?
05:23 - Priya: yes. rough numbers from the run: our per-response unit cost (median-length prompt) was 0.78x incumbent using quant+cache. Without quant it's 1.05x. I'll put a per-1M token breakdown in the pricing delta.
05:36 - Liam: remember our constraint: peak bursts up to 500 concurrent reqs for short windows — can you simulate bursts?
05:42 - Priya: we did a burst test: with autoscale + sustained dedicated slots, we can handle a 500-client spike for up to 90s before we need additional burst capacity; p95 degrades to ~620ms during that period. With a warmed dedicated slot and higher batch window it falls to ~420ms.
06:04 - Ethan: so recommendation is a hybrid: keep minimal dedicated slot for the peak 90s window and rely on hosted autoscale for overflow. That gives cost control and better p95.
06:16 - Daniel: how quickly does the dedicated slot warm back after idling? is there a keepalive requirement?
06:21 - Priya: depends on idle time; we have an idle TTL setting. with TTL set to 10 minutes, you get near-warm start; zero TTL means full cold startup. We'll recommend 10 min for your workload.
06:33 - Sofia: ok what's the proposed next bench we agreed?
06:36 - Priya: run three targeted microbenchmarks: (1) cold-start p95 with KV cold (2) same with KV primed (prefix warming) (3) burst 500 concurrent baseline vs warmed dedicated slot. We'll capture per-token timings and kernel-init breakdown.
06:52 - Liam: and we want raw logs, not aggregated so we can correlate with our tracing.
06:55 - Priya: yes we'll share CSVs and flamegraphs.
07:00 - Ethan: action items — I'll send pricing delta and slot config; Priya will send security docs and run microbench; customer will share canonical prompts and burst profile. Anything else?
07:12 - Sofia: can we get a small demo of the console dashboards after the docs come through?
07:15 - Ethan: absolutely, we'll schedule a 30-min console walkthrough next week.
07:19 - Daniel: one more ops q — if we go private deployment later, will the same tuning knobs apply?
07:24 - Priya: yes the runtime and knobs are consistent across hosted, dedicated and private. quantization profiles and kernel selection are identical; you'd just manage infra. there might be slight differences in network latency.
07:36 - Liam: ok wrap up then, thanks all.

Recap: Redwood shows better median latency, throughput advantage when using 4-bit quant and batching; tail gap due to cold starts. Plan to run cold vs warmed microbench, try prefix warming, evaluate dedicated slot for peak bursts. Deliver security docs, pricing delta, raw bench logs, and console demo.

End of transcript.
